fullPassage: By internalizing the opinions of others, we become intrinsically motivated. We do things because it feels right, which is why we are suspicious of others who have ulterior motives or who are extrinsically motivated. This is why paying people for their kindness backfires. Take blood donation. We do this without expectation of reward. In his book The Gift Relationship, comparing blood services in the US and the UK, the sociologist Richard Titmuss concluded that paying blood donors (as happens in the US) was not only dangerous, because it incentivized the wrong individuals and created dubious practices and safety concerns, but that if the practice was introduced in the UK, it would remove people's intrinsic motivation to express altruism, and erode the communal efforts that are the bedrock of the National Health Service. To test his claims, Swedish researchers carried out a study where adults were asked to donate blood voluntarily, or received the equivalent of $7 in payment, or could donate this payment to a charity. In line with Titmuss's prediction, blood donations dropped significantly when donors were offered payment, but not if the money could be donated to a charity. This phenomenon, known as 'crowding out', sullies the good intentions derived from helping others because it removes the intrinsic value we get, which is why rewarding people financially for acts that are supposed to be morally motivated is considered nasty. When blood donors and non-blood donors were tested with a charitable game, in which blood donors were told that their selected charity would receive no more and no less than $7, with the difference being made up by the experimenter running the study and thus their additional financial donations made no difference to the final amount received by the charity, blood donors still gave more relative to non-blood donors for the sheer warm glow they experienced.

questions.stem:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

Take blood donation. We do this without expectation of reward.

(A) In his book The Gift Relationship, comparing blood services in the US and the UK, the sociologist Richard Titmuss concluded that paying blood donors (as happens in the US) was not only dangerous, because it incentivized the wrong individuals and created dubious practices and safety concerns, but that if the practice was introduced in the UK, it would remove people's intrinsic motivation to express altruism, and erode the communal efforts that are the bedrock of the National Health Service.

(B) In line with Titmuss's prediction, blood donations dropped significantly when donors were offered payment, but not if the money could be donated to a charity.

(C) This phenomenon, known as 'crowding out', sullies the good intentions derived from helping others because it removes the intrinsic value we get, which is why rewarding people financially for acts that are supposed to be morally motivated is considered nasty.

det.korean: Titmuss의 경고(A) → 그 예측이 실제로 확인된 실험 결과(B) → 그 결과에 붙여진 이름인 crowding out 현상 설명(C) 순으로 전개된다.
det.analysis:
① (A) - (B) - (C) ← 정답
→ 도입문: 헌혈은 보상 없이 이루어진다는 배경 제시 → (A): Titmuss가 보상 도입 시 내재적 동기가 사라지고 공동체적 노력이 약화될 것이라고 경고(예측) → (B): "In line with Titmuss's prediction"으로 (A)의 예측이 실제로 확인되었음을 설명 → (C): "This phenomenon"으로 (B)에서 설명한 현상에 crowding out이라는 이름을 붙임

② (B) - (A) - (C)
→ (B)는 "In line with Titmuss's prediction"으로 시작하는데, Titmuss의 예측이 무엇인지 (A)에서 먼저 제시되어야 함. 도입문 직후에 (B)가 오면 예측의 내용을 알 수 없음

③ (A) - (C) - (B)
→ (C)의 "This phenomenon"은 보상 시 헌혈이 줄었다는 구체적 결과를 가리키는데, 그 결과가 (B)에 나오므로 (C)가 (B)보다 먼저 오면 지시 대상이 없음

④ (C) - (B) - (A)
→ (C)가 먼저 오면 "This phenomenon"이 가리킬 대상이 전혀 제시되지 않은 채 등장해 글이 성립하지 않음
det.tip: This phenomenon(C)은 바로 앞(B)에서 설명된 구체적 결과를 가리키는 지시어이다.

det.korean: 연구자들은 이 따뜻한 감정(warm glow)이 기부자의 추가 기부가 자선단체에 아무런 차이를 만들지 않아도 유지될지 궁금해했다는 문장으로, 뒤에 이어지는 자선 게임 연구를 도입한다.
det.analysis:

→ "this warm glow"와 "changed nothing for the charity"를 언급하므로, 바로 뒤에 그 구체적 실험(자선 게임, 차액이 고정된 $7)이 이어져야 한다.

① ( ① ) 뒤: 사람들이 숨은 동기를 의심한다는 내용 직후. 아직 헌혈·보상 이야기가 시작되지 않아 "warm glow"가 가리킬 대상이 없음

② ( ② ) 뒤: "Take blood donation" 직후. 아직 Titmuss의 연구나 자선 게임이 전혀 언급되지 않은 단계라 너무 이름

③ ( ③ ) 뒤: Titmuss의 경고 직후, 다음 문장("To test his claims")은 그 경고를 검증하는 스웨덴 연구로 바로 이어져야 함. 삽입 문장이 끼면 "his claims"와의 연결이 끊김

④ ( ④ ) 뒤 ← 정답
→ 앞: crowding out 현상 설명(보상이 내재적 가치를 없앤다)
→ 다음: "When blood donors and non-blood donors were tested with a charitable game ... made no difference to the final amount received by the charity, blood donors still gave more ... for the sheer warm glow they experienced."
→ 삽입 문장의 "this warm glow"와 "changed nothing for the charity"가 바로 다음 문장의 "no more and no less than $7", "made no difference", "warm glow"와 정확히 연결됨
det.tip: 지시어 "this warm glow"와 "changed nothing for the charity"가 가리키는 구체적 실험(자선 게임)이 바로 뒤에 와야 한다.

det.korean: '성공한다(succeeds)'가 아니라 '역효과를 낸다(backfires)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 보상이 친절을 베푸는 내재적 동기를 해친다는 글의 중심 주장과 반대된다.
det.analysis:
① succeeds → 원문은 backfires예요. 글 전체가 사람들에게 친절에 대해 돈을 주면 오히려 역효과(내재적 동기 상실)가 난다고 주장하므로, '성공한다(succeeds)'가 아니라 '역효과를 낸다(backfires)'가 맞아요 ←정답

② dangerous — paying blood donors was ... dangerous(헌혈자에게 돈을 주는 것은 위험하다), 문맥 일치

③ dropped — blood donations dropped significantly(헌혈이 크게 줄었다), 문맥 일치

④ removes — it removes the intrinsic value we get(그것은 우리가 얻는 내재적 가치를 없앤다), 문맥 일치

det.korean: '강화할(strengthen)'이 아니라 '약화시킬(erode)'이 문맥상 적절하다. Titmuss는 보상이 도입되면 공동체적 노력의 기반이 침식된다고 경고했다.
det.analysis:

questions.passage: By internalizing the opinions of others, we become intrinsically motivated. We do things because it feels right, which is why we are suspicious of others who have ulterior motives or who are extrinsically motivated. This is why paying people for their kindness backfires. Take blood donation. We do this without expectation of reward. In his book The Gift Relationship, comparing blood services in the US and the UK, the sociologist Richard Titmuss concluded that paying blood donors (as happens in the US) was not only dangerous, because it incentivized the wrong individuals and created dubious practices and safety concerns, but that if the practice was introduced in the UK, it would remove people's intrinsic motivation to express altruism, and erode the communal efforts that are the bedrock of the National Health Service. To test his claims, Swedish researchers carried out a study where adults were asked to donate blood voluntarily, or received the equivalent of $7 in payment, or could donate this payment to a charity. ① In line with Titmuss's prediction, blood donations dropped significantly when donors were offered payment, but not if the money could be donated to a charity. ② This phenomenon, known as 'crowding out', sullies the good intentions derived from helping others because it removes the intrinsic value we get, which is why rewarding people financially for acts that are supposed to be morally motivated is considered nasty. ③ Modern smartphone health apps allow users to track their daily step count with remarkable precision. ④ When blood donors and non-blood donors were tested with a charitable game, in which blood donors were told that their selected charity would receive no more and no less than $7, with the difference being made up by the experimenter running the study and thus their additional financial donations made no difference to the final amount received by the charity, blood donors still gave more relative to non-blood donors for the sheer warm glow they experienced.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?

det.korean: 이 글은 금전 보상이 선행의 내재적 동기를 해치는 크라우딩 아웃 현상을 다루는데, '스마트폰 건강 앱의 걸음 수 측정'에 관한 내용은 전체 흐름과 무관하다.
det.analysis:
① ①은 스웨덴 연구의 결과(보상 제안 시 헌혈 감소)를 설명하며 자연스럽게 이어진다.

② ②는 crowding out이라는 현상의 이름과 의미를 설명하며 자연스럽게 이어진다.

✅ ③ 스마트폰 건강 앱과 걸음 수 측정에 대한 내용은 금전 보상과 내재적 동기(크라우딩 아웃)라는 글의 중심 소재와 아무 관련이 없다 ←정답

④ ④는 보상이 결과에 영향을 주지 않을 때의 추가 실험(자선 게임)으로 자연스럽게 이어진다.
det.tip: 무관문장 문제는 글의 핵심 소재(여기서는 '금전 보상과 내재적 동기')와 전혀 다른 기술적 소재가 끼어 있는지 확인한다.

questions.passage: Take blood donation. We do this without expectation of reward. In his book The Gift Relationship, comparing blood services in the US and the UK, the sociologist Richard Titmuss __________ (conclude) that paying blood donors was not only dangerous.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 주어 Richard Titmuss가 단수이고 전체 글이 과거시제로 서술되므로 conclude를 과거형 concluded로 바꿔야 한다.
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞 주어는 the sociologist Richard Titmuss(단수)예요. 글 전체가 과거에 있었던 연구와 결론을 서술하는 과거시제이므로, conclude를 과거형 concluded로 바꿔야 해요.

'Titmuss concluded that ...'는 '티트머스는 ~라고 결론지었다'로 해석돼요.
det.tip: 과거시제 서술 + 단수 주어 → 동사원형에 -ed를 붙인 과거형: conclude → concluded

questions.passage: To test his claims, Swedish researchers carried out a study where adults were asked to donate blood voluntarily. In line with Titmuss's prediction, blood donations dropped significantly when donors __________ (offer) payment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 주어 donors가 보상을 '제안받는' 대상이므로 수동태로 바꿔 were offered로 써야 한다.
det.analysis:
빈칸의 주어는 donors예요. 기부자들이 보상을 '제안하는' 것이 아니라 '제안받는' 것이므로 수동 관계예요. 그래서 offer를 수동태 과거형 were offered로 바꿔야 해요.

'when donors were offered payment'는 '기부자들이 보상을 제안받았을 때'로 해석돼요.
det.tip: 주어와 수동 관계 + 과거시제 → be동사 과거형 + p.p.: offer → were offered
